reviews.author: crivetimihai
reviews.body:
Nice work, Martin — this fills an important gap where query/header mappings were fully wired through the schema, DB, admin UI, and tool CRUD paths but weren't being applied during actual REST invocation.

**What the PR does well:**
- `apply_mapping_into_target()` is clean and well-scoped — pure function, no side effects, easy to reason about
- Cache payload propagation follows the established pattern (extract to locals before DB close)
- Only activates for REST integration type, consistent with schema validation

**Changes I made during rebase/review:**
- Rebased onto current `main` and resolved two merge conflict regions in the test file (mapping tests collided with recently-added retry/timeout tests)
- Squashed the 10 PR commits into a single clean commit preserving your authorship
- **Fixed 2 test regressions** in `TestRustMcpExecutionPlan` — the mock tool `SimpleNamespace` objects were missing `query_mapping`/`header_mapping` attributes needed after they were added to `_build_tool_cache_payload`
- **Added 9 unit tests** for `apply_mapping_into_target` covering: key renaming, target merging, overwrite semantics, `None`/empty mapping handling, unmapped key exclusion, and input immutability
- Added assertions verifying `query_mapping`/`header_mapping` presence in `_build_tool_cache_payload` output
- Removed spurious `query_mapping`/`header_mapping` from gateway mock (gateways don't have these fields)
- Applied Black formatting

All 285 tests in `test_tool_service.py` pass.

**One design note for awareness** (not blocking): when `query_mapping` is set, only explicitly mapped argument fields are included in the outgoing payload — unmapped fields are excluded. This differs from the no-mapping path which preserves all fields. This is reasonable for the REST passthrough use case (precise control over what gets sent), and I've added a test that documents this behavior explicitly.

LGTM — approving.

commits.message:
fix(api): apply query and header mappings on tool invocation (#1405)

When a tool has query_mapping or header_mapping configured, apply those
mappings during REST tool invocation so that argument fields are correctly
translated into query parameters and HTTP headers.

Closes #1405

Signed-off-by: Mihai Criveti <crivetimihai@gmail.com>

commits.message:
fix(api): harden query/header mapping with security validation, type guards, and tests

Tighten Dict[str, Any] to Dict[str, str] for query_mapping and header_mapping
in schemas, DB model, and Pydantic validation. Add schema-level size constraints
(max 50 entries, 128 char keys/values) on ToolCreate and ToolUpdate.

At invocation time, validate header mapping targets against sensitive header
patterns (Authorization, Proxy-Authorization, X-API-Key, etc.) and RFC 7230
header name syntax to prevent auth header overwrite and CRLF injection. Add
isinstance guards with dict-content validation matching the tool_oauth_config
pattern, and wrap mapping call sites in try/except for clear error messages
when mappings are corrupt.

Includes debug-level logging for unmapped keys, improved docstrings and inline
comments, mock_tool fixture defaults, and test coverage for GET method,
empty-dict mappings, URL-template param availability in headers, sensitive
header rejection, CRLF injection rejection, and content validation.

Closes #1405
